Q1005786: The most densely populated municipality of Luanda, Angola.

Q1006338: Headquarters of Nadia district, West Bengal.

Q1028088: District of Shantou in eastern Guangdong.

Q1028116: County-level city in Jiangsu under Taizhou.

Part of the Eastern Economic Corridor with the Laem Chabang port.
Q140304: Capital of Sharqia Governorate in the eastern Nile Delta.
Next to Bubastis (Tell Basta), the ancient city of the cat goddess Bastet.
A centre of the cotton and grain trade; home of Zagazig University.
Q140631: The oldest city in Taiwan, in the southwest; capital of Taiwan for over 200 years until 1887.
The Dutch built Fort Zeelandia here in 1624; Koxinga drove them out in 1662.
Has more temples than any other Taiwanese city; called the 'Phoenix City'.
Known for its traditional snacks and the Anping Old Fort.
Q14126: Capital of West Nusa Tenggara on the island of Lombok, Indonesia.
Gateway to Mount Rinjani, Lombok's volcano, and the Gili Islands.
Has Hindu Balinese temples like Pura Meru alongside a Muslim Sasak majority; known as an 'island of a thousand mosques'.
Q14168: Capital of West Kalimantan on Borneo, right on the equator.
The Equator Monument marks the line; at the equinox objects cast no shadow.
Founded in 1771 as a Malay sultanate; has a large Chinese (Teochew and Hakka) community.
Lies on the Kapuas, Indonesia's longest river.
Q14182: The largest city of South Kalimantan, on the Barito and Martapura rivers.
Called the 'City of a Thousand Rivers'.
Famous for its floating markets, like Lok Baintan.
Q1425428: City on the Tyne in North East England.
Grew around a Roman fort on Hadrian's Wall and a castle built in 1080.
A world centre of coal shipping and shipbuilding in the Industrial Revolution ('carrying coals to Newcastle').
Famous for its seven bridges over the Tyne and its football club.
Q142811: Pennsylvania's third city, in the Lehigh Valley.
The Liberty Bell was hidden here in 1777 to save it from the British.
With Bethlehem, home of Bethlehem Steel and the 'Christmas City', and Easton, it forms the Lehigh Valley urban area.
Q144663: Second-largest city of Hunan, on the Xiang River.
Mount Heng (Nanyue), one of China's Five Great Mountains, is nearby.
Site of the 1944 Defence of Hengyang, one of the longest battles of the war against Japan.
Legend says wild geese flying south stop at its Huiyan peak.
Q14499: Capital of East Kalimantan, the most populous city on Borneo.
Lies on the Mahakam River; grew with timber, coal and oil.
Near the site of Nusantara, Indonesia's planned new capital.
Q1452991: City near Agra in Uttar Pradesh.
The centre of India's glass industry, especially glass bangles.
Named after Firoz Shah, an officer of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
Q1461: Capital of the Philippines, on Manila Bay on the island of Luzon; one of the most densely populated cities proper in the world.
Spanish conquistador Legazpi built the walled city of Intramuros here in 1571.
The Manila galleons linked Asia with Spanish America (Acapulco) for 250 years, making it one of the first global trade cities.
Metro Manila also includes Quezon City, which has more people than Manila itself.
Q14634: Capital of South Sulawesi, the largest city of eastern Indonesia; called Ujung Pandang from 1971 to 1999.
Centre of the Gowa Sultanate, which the Dutch conquered in the 17th century; Fort Rotterdam survives.
Makassarese sailors fished for sea cucumbers as far as northern Australia.
Known for its Losari Beach sunsets and phinisi wooden sailing ships.
Q1467: Capital of Cebu province in the Visayas; the oldest city of the Philippines.
Magellan landed here in 1521 and planted a cross (Magellan's Cross) — and was killed by chief Lapulapu on nearby Mactan.
The first Spanish settlement in the Philippines (1565) under Legazpi.
The Basilica del Santo Niño holds the oldest Christian relic in the country; the Sinulog festival is held every January.
Q146723: Capital of Tshopo province in DR Congo, on the Congo River near Boyoma Falls.
Formerly Stanleyville, named after the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.
The furthest point upriver navigable from Kinshasa; Joseph Conrad's 'Heart of Darkness' was inspired by a trip here.
Was a centre of Patrice Lumumba's movement.
Q147187: Site of the 1938 Battle of Taierzhuang, the first major Chinese victory over Japan in WWII.
Its Taierzhuang ancient town on the Grand Canal has been rebuilt.
Q1473: The largest city in the Philippines by area and the biggest city on Mindanao.
Near Mount Apo, the highest mountain in the Philippines.
Home region of the Philippine eagle and known for durian.
Hometown of President Rodrigo Duterte, its long-time mayor.
Q147402: The most populous municipality of Jalisco, part of the Guadalajara metro area.
Its Basilica holds the 16th-century Virgin of Zapopan; every October a huge procession brings her back.
Home of the Estadio Akron of Chivas Guadalajara.
The name means 'among the sapote trees'.
Q1475: The most populous city of the Philippines, part of Metro Manila.
Founded in 1939 and named after President Manuel L. Quezon; capital of the Philippines from 1948 to 1976.
Home of the University of the Philippines and many TV networks.
The 1986 People Power Revolution took place on EDSA avenue, partly in Quezon City.
Q1477270: The municipality of Mexicali, the northernmost municipality of Latin America.
Includes the city of Mexicali and the Mexicali Valley farmland, irrigated by the Colorado River.
Also contains islands in the Gulf of California.
Q14773: A special administrative region of China across the Pearl River estuary from Hong Kong; the most densely populated region in the world.
A Portuguese trading post from 1557 and colony until 1999 — the last European colony in Asia.
The world's biggest gambling centre, earning more from casinos than Las Vegas.
Its historic centre, with the ruins of St. Paul's, is a World Heritage Site; known for Portuguese egg tarts.
Q1478: City in Metro Manila, the fourth-most populous in the Philippines.
Birthplace of the Katipunan revolution: Andrés Bonifacio started the 1896 revolt against Spain here.
Split into two separate parts after Quezon City took much of its land in 1949.
Q1479: City on the Garonne in southwestern France, capital of Nouvelle-Aquitaine.
World capital of wine: the Bordeaux region includes Médoc and Saint-Émilion.
Its 18th-century 'Port of the Moon' centre is a World Heritage Site.
Has the Water Mirror in front of the Place de la Bourse and the Cité du Vin museum.
Q147975: City in Kaduna State, one of the original seven Hausa city-states (Zazzau).
Home of Ahmadu Bello University, Nigeria's largest university.
Associated with Queen Amina of Zazzau, a 16th-century warrior queen.
Q1480013: Metro area in Minnesota around the meeting of the Mississippi, Minnesota and St. Croix rivers, called the 'Twin Cities'.
Minneapolis grew as the flour-milling capital of the world at St. Anthony Falls; Saint Paul is the state capital.
Home of the Mall of America, one of the largest malls in the US.
The murder of George Floyd in Minneapolis in 2020 sparked worldwide protests.
Q1486: Capital of Argentina, on the Río de la Plata estuary; its residents are called porteños ('port people').
Home of the tango, which developed in its working-class neighbourhoods around 1900.
Millions of European immigrants, mostly Italians and Spaniards, arrived from the 19th century onward.
Avenida 9 de Julio, one of the widest avenues in the world, runs past the Obelisk.
Q1489: Capital of Mexico, at 2,240 m in the Valley of Mexico.
Built on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, which stood on an island in Lake Texcoco; the drained lakebed makes the city sink.
Its Zócalo is one of the largest city squares in the world, next to the Metropolitan Cathedral.
Divided into 16 boroughs (alcaldías); has more museums than almost any other city.
Q1490: Capital of Japan and seat of the Emperor, at the head of Tokyo Bay on Honshu.
Originally called Edo; it became the seat of the Tokugawa shogunate in 1603 and was renamed Tokyo ('eastern capital') in 1868.
Governed as a prefecture-like 'Metropolis' with 23 special wards, including Shinjuku and Shibuya.
Hosted the Summer Olympics in 1964 and 2021.
Q1491: Seat of government of Bolivia, in a canyon at about 3,600 m; the official capital is Sucre.
The highest seat of government in the world, overlooked by the snowy Illimani mountain.
Its Mi Teleférico cable-car network is the longest urban cable car system in the world.
Forms a metro area with El Alto on the plateau above.
Q1492: Capital of Catalonia, on Spain's Mediterranean coast; Spain's second city.
Antoni Gaudí's buildings, including the still unfinished Sagrada Família basilica, define its look.
Its Eixample district, with octagonal blocks, was planned by Ildefons Cerdà in the 1860s.
Hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics; home of FC Barcelona.
Q15121208: Municipality in the State of Mexico, the most populous suburb of Mexico City.
The name means 'windy hill' in Nahuatl, after the wind god Ehecatl.
José María Morelos, hero of independence, was executed here in 1815.
Q1513: The largest city of central India, in Maharashtra; called the 'Orange City' for its orange farming.
Founded in 1702 by a Gond king; later capital of the Bhonsle Marathas and of the Central Provinces.
Lies near the geographic centre of India — the 'Zero Mile Stone' marks it.
Here B. R. Ambedkar converted to Buddhism with hundreds of thousands of followers in 1956.
Q1515: The largest city and economic capital of Côte d'Ivoire, on lagoons along the Gulf of Guinea.
Capital until 1983, when Yamoussoukro became the official capital; most institutions and embassies stayed in Abidjan.

One of the largest French-speaking cities in the world; known for its Plateau business district.
Q15174: A city in Guangdong bordering Hong Kong, grown from fishing villages since 1979.
China's first Special Economic Zone under Deng Xiaoping's reforms, often called the 'Silicon Valley of hardware'.
Headquarters of Huawei, Tencent, BYD and DJI; home to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Its port is among the busiest container ports in the world.
Q1519: Capital of the United Arab Emirates, on a T-shaped island in the Persian Gulf.
The richest emirate, holding most of the UAE's oil; its sovereign wealth fund is among the largest in the world.
Landmarks: the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and the Louvre Abu Dhabi.
Hosts the Abu Dhabi Formula 1 Grand Prix on Yas Island.
Q151958: City in Hunan on the east shore of Dongting Lake where it joins the Yangtze.
The Yueyang Tower is one of the 'Three Great Towers' of southern China, made famous by Fan Zhongyan's essay.
Junshan island in the lake grows the rare Junshan Yinzhen yellow tea.
Hunan's only Yangtze port open to international trade.
Q1520: Capital of Kazakhstan since 1997, on the Ishim River in the steppe; the name means 'capital'.
Called Akmolinsk, Tselinograd and, from 2019 to 2022, Nur-Sultan.
Rebuilt with futuristic buildings like the Bayterek Tower and the tent-shaped Khan Shatyr.
One of the coldest capitals in the world, with winters below −30 °C.
Q1524: Capital of Greece and one of the oldest cities in the world, with over 3,400 years of recorded history.
Birthplace of democracy and centre of classical Greek philosophy (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle).
The Acropolis with the Parthenon is a World Heritage Site.
Hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896 and again in 2004.
Q1525057: City in West Bengal on the Mahananda River, also called English Bazar.
Famous for mangoes (e.g. Fazli) and silk.
Near the ruins of Gauda and Pandua, old capitals of medieval Bengal.
Q152831: City in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq near the Turkish border.
Capital of Duhok Governorate, in a valley of the Zagros foothills.
Hosted many refugee camps for Yazidis and Syrians after 2014; the Duhok Dam is nearby.
Q1530: Capital of Iraq, on the Tigris River.
Founded in 762 by Caliph al-Mansur as the round city of the Abbasid Caliphate; home of the House of Wisdom.

Q1533: Capital of Venezuela, in a valley at about 900 m, separated from the Caribbean by the Ávila mountain.
Birthplace of Simón Bolívar, the liberator of much of South America.
Founded in 1567 by the Spanish as Santiago de León de Caracas.
Grew rich with oil in the 20th century; its hillside slums are called barrios.
Q1538: City in Maharashtra on the Deccan Plateau, about 150 km southeast of Mumbai; formerly spelled Poona.
Seat of the Peshwas, prime ministers of the Maratha Empire, in the 18th century; Shaniwar Wada was their palace.
Called the 'Oxford of the East' for its universities; a big IT and car-manufacturing hub.
Gandhi was interned at the Aga Khan Palace here in 1942–44.
Q1555: Capital of Guatemala, the largest city in Central America, in a highland valley.
Founded in 1776 after an earthquake destroyed the old capital, Antigua Guatemala.
The Maya city of Kaminaljuyu lay on its site.
Surrounded by active volcanoes such as Pacaya and Volcán de Fuego.
Q1557962: Town in Bhadohi district, Uttar Pradesh.
Bhadohi is India's 'carpet city': a major centre of hand-knotted carpet weaving.
Q1563: Capital of Cuba, on the north coast facing the Florida Straits.
Founded by the Spanish in 1519; for centuries the treasure fleets gathered here before sailing to Spain.
Old Havana and its fortifications are a World Heritage Site; known for 1950s American cars and the Malecón seawall.
Centre of the 1959 revolution of Fidel Castro.
Q156819: The largest city in Santa Catarina state in southern Brazil.
Founded in 1851 by German, Swiss and Norwegian immigrants; named after the Prince of Joinville.
Hosts the only Bolshoi Ballet school outside Russia and a big dance festival.
Called the 'City of Flowers' and the 'City of Bicycles'.
Q1580709: Large township on the East Rand of Gauteng, north of Kempton Park.
Established in 1957 under apartheid, when Black residents were moved from Alexandra and other areas.
Part of the Ekurhuleni metropolitan municipality.
Q158467: City in Madhya Pradesh dominated by Gwalior Fort on a hilltop.

Home of the Scindia dynasty; known as a centre of Hindustani classical music (Tansen's tomb).
The Jai Vilas Palace has huge chandeliers.
Q159273: Peru's second city, in a valley below the El Misti volcano.
Called the 'White City' for its buildings of white volcanic stone (sillar); its centre is a World Heritage Site.
Home of the Santa Catalina Monastery, a city within the city.
The 'Juanita' Inca ice mummy is kept here; gateway to the Colca Canyon.
Q160320: Capital of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, on the Persian Gulf.
Oil was first found in Saudi Arabia here in 1938 (Dammam No. 7 'Prosperity Well').

Connected to Bahrain by the King Fahd Causeway.
Q160450: Port city on Turkey's Black Sea coast.
Atatürk landed here on 19 May 1919 to begin the Turkish War of Independence.
Known for Bafra pide and its tobacco farms.
Q1624: City in eastern Metro Manila along the Pasig River.
Shares the Ortigas Center business district with Mandaluyong and Quezon City.
Founded in 1573 by Augustinian friars; its cathedral dates from then.
Q162442: City in Uttar Pradesh, formerly Allahabad, at the confluence (Sangam) of the Ganges, Yamuna and mythical Sarasvati.

Birthplace of Jawaharlal Nehru; centre of the Indian independence movement.
Seat of the Allahabad High Court, one of the oldest in India.
Q162880: City in northwestern Shandong on the Grand Canal.
Called 'China's Solar Valley' for its solar water heater industry.
The tomb of a 15th-century king of Sulu (Philippines), who died while visiting China, is here.
Q1629: City at the southwestern tip of Mindanao, Philippines.
Called 'Asia's Latin City': many people speak Chavacano, a Spanish-based creole.
Fort Pilar was built by the Spanish in 1635.
Q1636: Capital of Rizal province, on the hills east of Metro Manila.
A pilgrimage city: the Antipolo Cathedral shrine of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage draws crowds every May.
Known for suman (sticky-rice snacks), cashews and views over Manila at night.
Q163798: City in central Kerala, called the 'cultural capital of Kerala'.
Built around a hill with the Vadakkunnathan Temple at its centre.
Famous for Thrissur Pooram, a temple festival with dozens of decorated elephants and fireworks.
Former capital of the Kingdom of Cochin.
Q1640079: Second city of Sindh, Pakistan, on the Indus about 150 km northeast of Karachi.
Founded in 1768 by the Kalhora ruler Ghulam Shah; capital of Sindh until the British conquest in 1843.
Known for its windcatchers on rooftops, bangles and the Pakka Qila fort.
Named after Hazrat Ali, also known as Haydar.
Q164234: City in Kanagawa between Tokyo and Yokohama.
The only Japanese city with over a million people that is not a prefectural capital.
Part of the Keihin industrial zone; home of Fujitsu and Toshiba plants.
Known for the Fujiko F. Fujio (Doraemon) Museum and the Kanamara Matsuri festival.
Q1643: City in Metro Manila with Bonifacio Global City, a modern business district on a former army base.
Hosts many embassies and corporate headquarters.
Lies between Laguna de Bay and the Pasig River.
Q1645: The main city of Northern Mindanao, Philippines; the name means 'Cagayan of Gold'.
Known for white-water rafting on the Cagayan de Oro River.
Called the 'City of Golden Friendship'; gateway to Camiguin and Bukidnon.
Q16520: South Korea's second city and main port, at the southeastern tip of the Korean Peninsula.

Known for Haeundae Beach, the hillside Gamcheon Culture Village and Jagalchi fish market.

Q165204: Capital of Yucatán, Mexico, near the Gulf coast.
Founded in 1542 on the Maya city of T'ho; its cathedral is the oldest on the American mainland.
Called the 'White City' for its limestone buildings; one of Mexico's safest cities.
Gateway to Chichén Itzá, Uxmal and the cenotes.
Q165341: Capital of Piauí, the only northeastern Brazilian state capital not on the coast.
Founded in 1852 as one of Brazil's first planned cities; named after Empress Teresa Cristina.
Called the 'Green City' for its trees; one of the hottest cities in Brazil.
Lies between the Parnaíba and Poti rivers.
Q16552: City on the Pacific in Southern California, right next to the Mexican border and Tijuana.
Called the 'Birthplace of California': the first Spanish mission in California was founded here in 1769.
Home of a large US Navy base and the famous San Diego Zoo.
Known for its mild climate, beaches and Balboa Park.
Q16553: The largest city in the Bay Area and the 'Capital of Silicon Valley'.
Founded in 1777 as the first civilian Spanish town in California; it was California's first state capital.
Home of tech companies like Cisco, Adobe and Zoom.
Known for the mysterious Winchester Mystery House.
Q16554: Capital of Colorado, at the foot of the Rocky Mountains.
Called the 'Mile High City': it lies about one mile (1,609 m) above sea level.
Founded in 1858 during the Pike's Peak Gold Rush.
Gateway to the Rocky Mountain ski resorts.
Q16555: The largest city in Texas and the fourth-largest in the USA, near the Gulf of Mexico.
Named after Sam Houston, who won Texas independence from Mexico in 1836.

Home of the Texas Medical Center, the world's largest medical complex.
Q16556: Capital of Arizona, in the Sonoran Desert; the most populous US state capital.
Founded in 1867 on the ruins of ancient Hohokam irrigation canals, so named after the mythical bird rising from ashes.
One of the hottest big cities in the USA, often above 40 °C in summer.

Q16557: The third-largest city in Texas, core of the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex.

Q16558: Texas's fourth-largest city, part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex.

Home to the Kimbell Art Museum and a major US money-printing facility.
Q16559: Capital of Texas, on the Colorado River in the Texas Hill Country.

Q16562: City in West Texas on the Rio Grande, across from Ciudad Juárez, Mexico.
Named after the mountain pass 'El Paso del Norte'.
Home of Fort Bliss, one of the largest US Army bases.
Mostly Hispanic and known for Tex-Mex food.
Q16563: City in Tennessee on the Mississippi River.
Birthplace of blues on Beale Street and of rock 'n' roll; Elvis Presley's Graceland is here.
Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated at the Lorraine Motel in 1968, now a civil rights museum.
Headquarters of FedEx, whose hub makes Memphis airport one of the busiest cargo airports.
Q16565: The largest city in North Carolina; named after Queen Charlotte, wife of King George III.
The second-largest banking centre in the US, headquarters of Bank of America.
Home of the NASCAR Hall of Fame; much of NASCAR is based nearby.
Q16567: Capital of Ohio and its largest city, where the Scioto and Olentangy rivers meet.
Named after Christopher Columbus; founded in 1812 as the planned state capital.
Home of Ohio State University, one of the largest universities in the US.
Often used as a test market for new products because it is so 'average'.
Q16568: The most populous city in Florida, on the St. Johns River near the Atlantic.
The largest city by area in the contiguous United States after merging with Duval County in 1968.
A big US Navy and logistics hub.
Q16572: Capital of Guangdong on the Pearl River, historically known in the West as Canton.

Centre of the Greater Bay Area with Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau; home of the Canton Fair, China's biggest trade fair.
Cantonese cuisine and dim sum come from this region.
Q1658159: City and local government area in Lagos State, northeast of Lagos.
Lies on the Lagos Lagoon next to Ogun State.
One of the fastest-growing parts of the Lagos region.
Q165972: Coastal city in Florida, about 50 km north of Miami.
Called the 'Venice of America' for its 300 km of canals.
Named after a 19th-century fort of the Seminole Wars.
Its Port Everglades is a major cruise port; famous as a spring break spot.
Q16665884: Metropolitan authority in southeastern France around Marseille and Aix-en-Provence, created in 2016.

Aix-en-Provence is the city of the painter Cézanne.
Known for bouillabaisse, Marseille soap and the Calanques national park.
Q16666: Capital of Jiangsu on the Yangtze; the name means 'southern capital'.
Capital of several Chinese dynasties and of the Republic of China; Sun Yat-sen's mausoleum is here.
Site of the Nanjing Massacre by Japanese troops in 1937–38.
Its Ming-dynasty city wall is one of the longest surviving city walls in the world.
Q167436: Capital of Paraíba in northeast Brazil.
Has the easternmost point of the Americas, Ponta do Seixas.
Founded in 1585, one of the oldest cities in Brazil; renamed after a murdered governor in 1930.
Known for its green spaces and beaches; a UNESCO City of Crafts.
Q167715: Capital of Kerala, near India's southern tip; formerly called Trivandrum.
Capital of the Kingdom of Travancore.
The Padmanabhaswamy Temple held a hidden treasure worth billions, discovered in 2011.
Home of the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, India's main rocket development centre.
Q167800: City in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq near the Turkish border.
Its Delal Bridge, an old stone bridge, is a landmark.
Close to the Ibrahim Khalil border crossing, Iraq's main gate to Turkey.
Had a famous Jewish community until 1951; known for Newroz celebrations.
Q168193: Holy city of Shia Islam, about 160 km south of Baghdad.
Burial place of Ali, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet; his shrine has a golden dome.
Wadi-us-Salaam is the largest cemetery in the world.
Its Hawza is a leading Shia seminary; home of Grand Ayatollah Sistani.
Q168376: Capital of Espírito Santo, mostly on an island in a bay.
Founded in 1551, one of the oldest cities in Brazil.
A major port for iron ore exports from Minas Gerais.
Known for the Convento da Penha in neighbouring Vila Velha and for moqueca capixaba (fish stew in clay pots).
Q168652: Capital of the self-declared Republic of Somaliland, which is internationally considered part of Somalia.
Grew as a watering and trading stop of the Isaaq clans.
Almost destroyed by Siad Barre's air force in 1988 during the civil war.
Near the Laas Geel caves with some of Africa's oldest rock paintings.
Q168866: University city in northwestern Turkey on the Porsuk River; the name means 'old city'.
Known for meerschaum stone, used to carve pipes.
Odunpazarı, its Ottoman wooden-house quarter, is a tourist attraction.
Has a high-speed train to Ankara and Istanbul.
Q168888: Capital of Alagoas in northeast Brazil, on the Atlantic.
Known for turquoise beaches and natural reef pools.
Has suffered land subsidence caused by rock-salt mining under several neighbourhoods.
Q168929: Capital of Mato Grosso do Sul in central-west Brazil.
A planned city with wide, tree-lined avenues; called the 'Brunette City' for its red soil.
Gateway to the Pantanal wetlands and Bonito.
Has large Japanese (Okinawan) and Paraguayan communities — known for sobá noodles.
Q169134: Capital of Nara Prefecture; Japan's capital from 710 to 784.
Tōdai-ji temple houses a giant bronze Buddha in one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.
About 1,000 sacred deer roam freely in Nara Park and bow for crackers.

Q16959: Capital of Xinjiang in China's far northwest, at the foot of the Tian Shan mountains.
Often called the city farthest from any ocean in the world (about 2,500 km).
An old stop on the northern Silk Road; home to Uyghurs, Han Chinese, Kazakhs and others.
Was called Dihua until 1954; the name means 'beautiful pasture' in Mongolian.
Q170115: Summer capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, on the Jhelum River in the Kashmir Valley.

Famous for Kashmir shawls (pashmina), papier-mâché and saffron.
Located in the disputed Kashmir region claimed by both India and Pakistan.
Q170247: Capital of Shandong province, near the Yellow River.
Known as the 'City of Springs' for its 72 famous artesian springs, like Baotu Spring.
Mount Tai, one of China's five sacred mountains, lies just to the south.
Q170315: Hill city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, at about 1,250 m.
Founded in 1853 and named after the British officer James Abbott.
Home of the Pakistan Military Academy at Kakul.
Osama bin Laden was killed here by US forces in 2011.
Q170322: Port city in Shandong on the Yellow Sea; formerly spelled Tsingtao.

Home of the appliance maker Haier.

Q170366: Capital of Khuzestan in southwest Iran, on the Karun River, Iran's largest river.
Centre of Iran's oil industry; has a large Arab population.
Known for its many bridges over the Karun.
One of the hottest cities in the world, often above 50 °C in summer.
Q17042: City in the East Bay across from San Francisco.
Its port is one of the busiest container ports in the US.
Birthplace of the Black Panther Party (1966).
Known for its diverse population and Lake Merritt.
Q170525: City on Morocco's Atlantic coast at the foot of the Atlas, capital of the Souss-Massa region.
Destroyed by the 1960 earthquake and rebuilt as a modern beach resort.

Considered a capital of Amazigh (Berber) culture and of argan oil.
Q170573: Holy city of Shia Islam, about 140 km south of Tehran.

The world's largest centre of Shia religious scholarship; Ayatollah Khomeini taught here.
Known for a pistachio-brittle sweet called sohan.
Q170578: Capital of Sergipe, Brazil's smallest state.
Founded in 1855 as a planned capital with a grid of streets.
Known for its long Atalaia beach and crab dishes.
Q170616: Capital of Chiba Prefecture on Tokyo Bay, east of Tokyo.

Q170688: Bolivia's largest city, in the tropical eastern lowlands.

Q1707092: Twin cities in northern Karnataka; Hubli is the commercial centre, Dharwad the seat of administration and education.

Q170967: Gateway to Pamukkale's white travertine terraces and the ruins of Hierapolis (World Heritage Site).

Famous for the Denizli rooster, a long-crowing breed.
Q17151: Greece's second city, on the Thermaic Gulf in Macedonia.

Q171617: City in São Paulo state, about 90 km northwest of São Paulo.

Q171632: Venezuela's second-largest city, on the strait linking Lake Maracaibo with the Caribbean.

Q171771: Capital of Odisha, called the 'Temple City of India' for its hundreds of old Hindu temples.

Q1718: Capital of North Rhine-Westphalia on the Rhine.

Famous for Altbier and its long Rhine promenade; rival of Cologne.
Q171943: Capital of Jiangxi province, near Poyang Lake, China's largest freshwater lake.

Q172: Canada's largest city and capital of Ontario, on the shore of Lake Ontario.

Q1726: Capital of Bavaria on the Isar River, north of the Alps; Germany's third-largest city.

Q173121: Capital of the state of Querétaro in Mexico's Bajío region.

Q173270: Mexico's oldest and most important port, on the Gulf of Mexico.

Famous for son jarocho music and its café culture.
Q173310: City in northern Iraq with a mix of Kurds, Turkmens and Arabs.

Q173545: City on the Orontes River in west-central Syria.
Famous for its giant wooden water wheels (norias), some over 20 m high.

Known for halawet el jibn, a cheese-based sweet.
Q173985: Pakistan's third-largest city and main textile centre, in Punjab; formerly called Lyallpur.

Q174: Brazil's largest city and the most populous city in the Americas, capital of São Paulo state.

Q174091: Capital of Hunan province, on the Xiang River.

Q1741: Capital of Austria on the Danube, at the edge of the Vienna Woods.

Q1741227: Includes the Kilamba new city, a huge housing project built by Chinese companies around 2011.

Q174461: Capital of Jharkhand, on the Chota Nagpur Plateau.

Called the 'City of Waterfalls' for falls like Hundru and Dassam nearby.
Hometown of cricket captain MS Dhoni.
Q174691: Capital of Shizuoka Prefecture, between Tokyo and Nagoya.

Q1748: Capital of Denmark, on the islands of Zealand and Amager.

Q1754: Capital of Sweden, built on 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.

Q1757: Capital of Finland, on the Gulf of Finland; called Helsingfors in Swedish.

Q1758751: New town in the northwestern New Territories of Hong Kong, also called Castle Peak.

Q1761: Capital of Ireland, at the mouth of the River Liffey on Dublin Bay.

Q17633266: Metro area in Anzoátegui state, Venezuela, joining Barcelona, Puerto La Cruz, Guanta and Lechería.

Q1774: Semi-autonomous archipelago of Tanzania off East Africa, called the 'Spice Islands'.

Q1781: Capital of Hungary, formed in 1873 from Buda and Óbuda on the hilly west bank and Pest on the flat east bank of the Danube.

Q178945: City in northeastern Sichuan; the name means 'centre of Ba'.

Q1794: Germany's financial centre on the Main River.

Q179608: Capital of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region in southern China, near Vietnam.

Q179665: Capital of West Azerbaijan province in northwestern Iran, near Turkey and Iraq.

Q1800: Port city on Kerala's Malabar Coast, formerly Cochin; called the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea'.

Q180078: City in western Iran, a centre of Kurdish culture.

Q18013: Capital of California, where the Sacramento and American rivers meet.

Q180921: Sudan's second city, on the west bank of the Nile opposite Khartoum.

Q181557: Taiwan's third city and main port, in the south of the island.

Q181966: Capital of Okinawa Prefecture, on Okinawa Island.

Q182059: Ghana's second-largest city, capital of the Ashanti Region.

Q182852: Capital of Yunnan province, at 1,900 m on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau.

Q183124: Bolivia's fourth city, in a fertile Andean valley at about 2,500 m.

Q183584: Capital of Gansu province, on the Yellow River in northwestern China.

Q18383: Capital of Rhode Island, at the head of Narragansett Bay.

Q184403: Municipality in the São Paulo metro area (the 'ABC region').

Q184409: City in São Paulo's metro area, the most populous Brazilian city that is not a state capital.

Q18459: Fast-growing city in Gyeonggi Province, south of Seoul.

Q1850: Capital of Cambodia, where the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers meet.

Q185458: Capital of Balochistan, Pakistan, in a mountain valley at about 1,680 m.

Q185518: Myanmar's second city, on the Irrawaddy River.

Q185582: City in East Tennessee on the Tennessee River, in the Appalachians.

Q1856565: The metropolitan municipality around Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) on Algoa Bay, Eastern Cape.

Q185684: Capital of Anhui province, north of Chao Lake.

Q18575: Arizona's second city, in the Sonoran Desert surrounded by mountains.

Q1861984: City on the mainland part of Penang, Malaysia, across from George Town.

Q1891: Capital of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy.

Q189633: City in Guangxi on the Li River; the name means 'forest of osmanthus'.

Q192271: Capital of Guizhou province, at about 1,100 m on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau.

Q1926941: Town in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, home of the Bokaro Thermal Power Station.

Q193021: City on Guanabara Bay north of Rio de Janeiro.

Q194531: City in southwestern Hunan, formerly Baoqing.

Q197519: Famous for its apples and as the 'hometown of Chinese apples' in Yunnan.

A centre of the garment industry; the Rana Plaza factory collapse here in 2013 killed over 1,100 workers.
Q240: Capital of Belgium and the de facto capital of the European Union (European Commission, Council, Parliament).
Its Grand-Place, with ornate guild houses, is a World Heritage Site; the Atomium was built for Expo 58.
Officially bilingual (French and Dutch); known for waffles, chocolate, comics and the Manneken Pis.
Q242895: Deoband, home of the influential Darul Uloom Islamic seminary, is in the district.
Q243293: Twin city on Ghana's west coast, capital of the Western Region.
Grew from 17th-century Dutch and English forts.
Takoradi harbour (1928) was Ghana's first deep-water port.
Centre of Ghana's offshore oil industry since 2010 ('Oil City').
Q243322: City in Punjab, Pakistan, north of Lahore; nicknamed the 'City of Wrestlers'.
Birthplace of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, founder of the Sikh Empire, and its first capital.
One of Pakistan's main industrial centres, known for ceramics, fans and metal goods.
Q243325: Third-largest metro area of Bangladesh, on the Rupsha River.
Gateway to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest and home of the Bengal tiger.
Near the Port of Mongla and the Sixty Dome Mosque in Bagerhat (World Heritage Site).
Centre of shrimp farming and jute processing.
Q243327: Capital of South Gyeongsang Province, on Masan Bay.
Formed in 2010 by merging Changwon, Masan and Jinhae.
Changwon was one of Korea's first planned cities (1970s), built around a large machinery industrial complex.
Jinhae is famous for its cherry blossom festival.
Q243766: Capital of Santander department in Colombia.
Called the 'City of Parks' for its more than 160 parks.
Famous for eating hormigas culonas (big-bottomed ants).
Q243846: City in central Iraq on the Euphrates, next to the ruins of Babylon.
Capital of Babylon Governorate; founded around 1101.
Was a centre of Shia learning in the Middle Ages.
Nearby are ancient Borsippa and Kish.
Q244159: City in Jharkhand, called the 'Coal Capital of India' for the Jharia coalfield.
The Jharia coal fires have been burning underground for over 100 years.
Home of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, an old mining school.
Q244232: Capital of Tabuk Province in northwestern Saudi Arabia, near Jordan.
The Prophet Muhammad led an expedition here in 630.
A stop on the Hejaz Railway; near the planned NEOM mega-project.
A farming area known for roses and fruit.
Q244898: The most populous city of Taiwan, completely surrounding the capital Taipei.
Called Taipei County until it became a special municipality in 2010.
Includes the old port of Tamsui with the Spanish-built Fort San Domingo, and the mountain town of Jiufen.
Mostly a commuter city for Taipei; seat at Banqiao.
Q2449: Capital of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean; locally called Xamar.
A medieval trading sultanate that controlled the Indian Ocean gold trade; visited by Ibn Battuta.
Capital of Italian Somaliland; devastated by civil war from 1991, including the 1993 'Black Hawk Down' battle.
Q245023: Taiwan's second-largest city, in the Taichung Basin in central Taiwan.
Planned in the Qing era as the capital of Taiwan Province; laid out by the Japanese in a grid.
Birthplace of bubble tea (Chun Shui Tang teahouse claims it).
Known for its mild climate and the National Taichung Theater by Toyo Ito.
Q2460416: Industrial city just north of Dhaka, part of Greater Dhaka.
A hub of the Bangladeshi garment industry, with a large share of the country's clothing factories.
Home of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Safari Park and the Bhawal National Park.
Q24639: The largest city of British Columbia, on the Pacific between mountains and the sea.
Founded as a sawmill settlement; named after the British captain George Vancouver.
Home of Stanley Park and a big film industry ('Hollywood North').
Hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics; often ranked one of the most liveable cities.
Q2471: Capital of Yemen, at about 2,300 m in the highlands.
Claims to be one of the oldest inhabited cities in the world.
Its Old City, with multi-storey rammed-earth tower houses decorated with white gypsum, is a World Heritage Site.
Controlled by the Houthi movement since 2014, during the civil war.
Q2473939: Fast-growing suburb north of Cotonou in Benin.
Home of the University of Abomey-Calavi, Benin's main university.
Next to the lake village of Ganvié on Lake Nokoué.
Q2475171: The municipality of Chihuahua, seat of the state capital.
Covers a large area with almost 900 small localities beyond the city.
Q24826: Port city on the Mersey estuary in northwest England.
Grew rich from the Atlantic trade, including the slave trade, and as an emigration port to America.
Home of the first inter-city railway (to Manchester, 1830) and the Beatles.
Famous for its waterfront (Royal Albert Dock) and the football clubs Liverpool and Everton.
Q2485095: The municipality of Culiacán, the most populous in Sinaloa.
Includes the state capital and coastal farmland of the Culiacán valley.
Q249007: City in central Gansu on the Hexi Corridor of the Silk Road.
The famous bronze 'Flying Horse of Gansu' (Han dynasty) was found here.
Called Liangzhou in history; a centre of early Buddhism in China (Kumarajiva lived here).
Q251329: Second city of Bihar, sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains.
Hindus come to perform pinda daan rites for their ancestors at the Vishnupad Temple.
Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, is about 15 km away (World Heritage Site).
Q25247670: Town and block in Siwan district, Bihar.
Part of the densely populated Bhojpuri-speaking plain of western Bihar.
Hit by floods of the Daha River in 2001.
Q25282: Port city in central Vietnam, on the coast at the mouth of the Hàn River.
Called Tourane under the French; site of a large US base during the Vietnam War, where US Marines landed in 1965.
Known for its beaches, the Dragon Bridge and the Marble Mountains.
Gateway to Hội An and Huế, both World Heritage Sites.
Q255455: Winter capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, on the Tawi River.
Called the 'City of Temples', e.g. the Raghunath Temple.
Base for pilgrims to the Vaishno Devi shrine.
Former seat of the Dogra maharajas.
Q25563103: Capital of the Kakatiya dynasty (12th–14th centuries); its Kakatiya Arch is on Telangana's emblem.
Nearby Ramappa Temple is a World Heritage Site; the Thousand Pillar Temple is in the city.
Home of an NIT engineering institute.
Q2568315: Coastal town in Kerala at the mouth of the Bharathappuzha, Kerala's second-longest river.
Called the 'little Mecca of Kerala' for its role in Islamic learning; the Ponnani Juma Masjid dates from the 16th century.
An old port of the Zamorin kings.
Q26323: City in eastern Guangdong, part of the Chaoshan region.
Hometown of many overseas Chinese in Southeast Asia.
Known for jade processing at the Yangmei jade market and for Teochew culture.
Q2634: The largest city of southern Italy, on the Bay of Naples beneath the volcano Vesuvius.
Founded by Greeks as Neapolis ('new city'); its historic centre is a World Heritage Site.
Pompeii and Herculaneum, buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD, are nearby.
Q2656: Capital of Sicily, on the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Founded by the Phoenicians; capital of an Arab emirate and then of the Norman Kingdom of Sicily.
Its Arab-Norman buildings, like the Palatine Chapel and Monreale Cathedral, are a World Heritage Site.
Famous for street food like arancine and for its markets (Ballarò).
Q26590: The largest city of Chihuahua, on the Rio Grande across from El Paso, Texas.
Called El Paso del Norte until 1888; renamed after President Benito Juárez.
A major maquiladora factory city and one of the busiest border crossings.
Claims to be the birthplace of the burrito.
Q26600: The largest city on Kyushu, on Hakata Bay; Japan's closest big city to the Asian mainland.
Kublai Khan's Mongol invasion fleets were destroyed here in 1274 and 1281 (the 'kamikaze' divine winds).
Famous for Hakata tonkotsu ramen and street food stalls (yatai).
Formed from the merger of the castle town Fukuoka and the merchant town Hakata.
Q266014: City in southern Hunan where the Xiao and Xiang rivers meet.
The Tang writer Liu Zongyuan was exiled here and wrote the famous 'Eight Records of Yongzhou'.
The Nüshu script, a writing system used only by women, comes from Jiangyong county here.
Q269: Capital of Uzbekistan and the largest city of Central Asia.
An old Silk Road city whose name means 'stone city'.
Conquered by Russia in 1865; largely rebuilt in Soviet style after a big earthquake in 1966.
Its metro stations are famous for their decoration; the Khast Imam complex holds an early Quran manuscript.
Q269899: City in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra.
Known for the Ambadevi temple from which its name may come.
A cotton-trading centre; the reformer Sant Gadge Baba worked here.
Q269960: Egypt's fourth-largest city, on the northern edge of Cairo in Qalyubiyya.
One of Egypt's main industrial areas (textiles, chemicals).
The name means 'hamlet of the tent'.
Q270: Capital of Poland, on the Vistula.
Became the capital in 1596 when King Sigismund III moved from Kraków.
About 85% destroyed in WWII after the 1944 Warsaw Uprising; its Old Town was rebuilt and is a World Heritage Site.
Birthplace of Chopin and Marie Curie; the Palace of Culture and Science was a gift from Stalin.
Q270041: Yemen's main port on the Red Sea, capital of Hodeidah Governorate.
Most of Yemen's food and fuel imports arrive here.
Was the focus of fierce fighting in the civil war in 2018.
Q270176: City in northern Karnataka near Maharashtra and Goa; officially Belagavi.
Karnataka built a second legislature building, the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha, here.
Has a large army cantonment and is famous for 'kunda' milk sweets.
Long disputed between Marathi and Kannada speakers.
Q27136: The main city of Al-Ahsa, the world's largest oasis, in eastern Saudi Arabia.
Al-Ahsa has about 2.5 million date palms and is a World Heritage Site.
Known for its old souq, Ibrahim Palace and the Al-Qarah Mountain caves.
Q271619: Capital of Perak, Malaysia, in the Kinta Valley.
Boomed as the centre of the world's richest tin-mining area in the 19th century.
Known for colonial buildings, white coffee and limestone cave temples.
Called the 'City of Millionaires' for its tin-mining fortunes.
Q271771: Capital of Gharbia Governorate in the Nile Delta.
Its mosque of the Sufi saint Ahmad al-Badawi draws huge crowds to his yearly festival (mawlid).
Known for sweets and roasted chickpeas; home of Tanta University.
Q273014: Port city in Tamaulipas on the Pánuco River near the Gulf of Mexico.
During Mexico's first oil boom (around 1920) it was one of the busiest oil-export ports in the world.
Its centre has French-style balconied buildings; known for 'tortas de la barda'.
Q2733647: Small town (Nagar Panchayat) in Siwan district, Bihar.
Part of the densely populated Bhojpuri-speaking region of western Bihar.
Q274584: Honduras's industrial capital and second city, in the Sula Valley near the Caribbean.
The largest Central American city that is not a capital.
Known for its maquila garment factories.
Was once called one of the most violent cities in the world.
Q2750772: Commercial and industrial city in Anambra State, Nigeria.
Called the 'Japan of Africa' for its many local manufacturers.
Home of Innoson, Nigeria's first indigenous car maker.
Known for its huge motor-spare-parts market.
Q2761728: City in northern Karnataka, twin city of Hubballi.
An education centre with Karnatak University and an agricultural university.
Famous for Hindustani music (Gangubai Hangal, Bhimsen Joshi) and the Dharwad pedha sweet.
Q2768828: City in western Uttar Pradesh on the Delhi–Haridwar road.
Called the 'sugar bowl of Uttar Pradesh' for sugar cane and jaggery.
A big jaggery market and paper-making centre.
Q277966: Capital of Kasaï Province in DR Congo, near the Angolan border.
Founded as a diamond-mining town by the Forminière company in the early 20th century.
Lies where the Tshikapa and Kasai rivers meet.
Q2807: Capital of Spain, in the centre of the Iberian Peninsula at about 660 m on the Manzanares River.
Became the permanent seat of the Spanish court in 1561 under Philip II.
The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen museums form its 'Golden Triangle of Art'.
Home of football clubs Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid.
Q2841: Capital of Colombia, high in the Andes at about 2,600 m.
Founded in 1538 by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada on land of the Muisca people; capital of the Viceroyalty of New Granada.
Capital of Gran Colombia after Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819.
Known for the Gold Museum and the TransMilenio bus rapid transit system.
Q2844: Capital of Brazil since 1960, built from scratch on the central highlands to develop the interior.
Planned by Lúcio Costa with buildings by Oscar Niemeyer; seen from above, the plan looks like an airplane or bird.
Its modernist core is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Founded by President Juscelino Kubitschek, replacing Rio de Janeiro.
Q28441: Capital of Maranhão, on an island in the Atlantic.
The only Brazilian state capital founded by the French (1612), later taken by the Portuguese.
Its historic centre with tile-covered colonial houses is a World Heritage Site.
Known as Brazil's 'reggae capital' and for the Bumba Meu Boi festival.
Q2868: Capital of Peru, in a coastal desert on the Pacific; one of the driest capitals in the world.
Founded by Francisco Pizarro in 1535 as the 'City of Kings'; capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru.
Its historic centre is a World Heritage Site; it includes the port of Callao.
Known as a capital of Latin American cuisine, e.g. ceviche.
Q28729: City on the Malabar Coast of Kerala, also called Calicut — the origin of the word 'calico'.
Vasco da Gama landed here in 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India.
Medieval spice-trade port of the Zamorin kings, visited by Ibn Battuta and Zheng He.
UNESCO's first 'City of Literature' in India (2023).
Q2875992: City in Dhaka Division, Bangladesh, in the haor wetlands region.
The Sholakia Eidgah hosts one of the largest Eid prayer gatherings in South Asia.
Was a jute, rice and fish trading town on the rivers.
Q2887: Capital of Chile, in the Central Valley between the Andes and the Coastal Range.
Founded in 1541 by Pedro de Valdivia; the Plaza de Armas was its original centre.
Home to over a third of Chile's population and nearly half its economy.
The snow-capped Andes are visible from the city; the Gran Torre Santiago is South America's tallest building.
Q289693: The third-largest city of the UAE, next to Dubai.
Ruled by the Al Qasimi dynasty since the 18th century.
Called the UAE's cultural capital; UNESCO's Arab Capital of Culture in 1998.
Alcohol is banned in the emirate.
Q28979: Coal-mining city in southeastern Heilongjiang, near the Russian border.
Near Lake Khanka (Xingkai), shared with Russia.
A crater on the asteroid 253 Mathilde is named after it.
Q28994: City in northern Guizhou between Guiyang and Chongqing.
The 1935 Zunyi Conference during the Long March made Mao Zedong a leader of the Communist Party.
Maotai, home of China's most famous liquor (baijiu), is in the prefecture.
Known for its red-tourism sites and tea.
Q28996: Port city in western Liaoning on the Liaoxi Corridor between North China and Manchuria.
The 1948 Liaoshen Campaign of the Chinese Civil War was decided here.
Its port is China's northernmost seaport.
Q2900: Capital of Ecuador, at 2,850 m in the Andes — one of the highest capitals in the world.
Its colonial centre is one of the best-preserved in the Americas and was among the first World Heritage Sites (1978).
The equator line (Mitad del Mundo monument) runs just north of the city.
Overlooked by the active Pichincha volcano.
Q29003: City in eastern Heilongjiang on the Songhua River near the Russian border.
Gateway to the Sanjiang Plain, China's 'Great Northern Wilderness' turned farmland.
Home of the Hezhe people, a small fishing minority; Fuyuan, China's easternmost point, is in the prefecture.
Q29015: City in Sichuan famous for salt: brine wells have been drilled here for about 2,000 years.
The Shenhai Well (1835) was the first well in the world drilled deeper than 1,000 m.
Known for its Lantern Festival, its dinosaur museum and spicy food.
Q29109964: A 'new area' in Hebei about 100 km south of Beijing, launched in 2017 by Xi Jinping.
Being built as a planned city for government offices, companies and universities moved out of Beijing.
Includes Baiyangdian, the largest freshwater lake in northern China.
Planned to reach 5 million people by mid-century.
Q2933: Capital of Paraguay, on the Paraguay River opposite Argentina.
Founded in 1537: one of the oldest cities in South America, called the 'Mother of Cities' because expeditions from here founded others, including Buenos Aires (second time).
Most residents speak both Spanish and Guaraní.
Its metro area holds about a third of Paraguay's people.
Q29962: The largest city of Upper Egypt, on the Nile.
Has one of the largest Coptic Christian communities in Egypt.
Ancient Lycopolis, a centre of the jackal god Wepwawet; the philosopher Plotinus came from here.
The Asyut Barrage across the Nile dates from 1903.
Q30002: Capital of Sichuan province in western China, on the fertile Chengdu Plain ('Land of Abundance').
Home of the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding.
Kept the same name for over 2,000 years; capital of the Shu Han kingdom in the Three Kingdoms era.
A UNESCO City of Gastronomy, famous for spicy, numbing Sichuan pepper cuisine; the ancient Dujiangyan irrigation system is nearby.
Q300577: City in northern Tamil Nadu on the Palar River.
Its granite Vellore Fort (16th century) saw the 1806 Vellore Mutiny, an early revolt against British rule.
Home of the famous Christian Medical College hospital and VIT university.
The Golden Temple of Sripuram is nearby.
Q30340: Capital of Henan province on the south bank of the Yellow River, in the 'cradle of Chinese civilization'.
Site of an early Shang-dynasty capital about 3,600 years ago.
A key railway junction where China's main north–south and east–west lines cross; nicknamed 'iPhone City' for Foxconn's huge factory.
The Shaolin Temple, birthplace of Shaolin kung fu, is nearby.
Q3037: Capital of Nepal, at about 1,400 m in the Kathmandu Valley.
Historically the centre of the Newar people; the valley has seven World Heritage monuments, incl. Durbar Square, Swayambhunath and Boudhanath.
A starting point for treks in the Himalayas.
Q304848: Oil city in western Heilongjiang; the name means 'great celebration'.
Founded after the Daqing Oil Field was discovered in 1959, China's largest oil field.
Mao's slogan 'In industry, learn from Daqing' made it a national model.
Known for wetlands and many lakes in the grassland around it.
Q3070: Capital of Costa Rica, in the Central Valley.
Was one of the first cities in the world with public electric street lighting (1884).
Known for the National Theatre and the pre-Columbian Gold Museum.
Q3110: Capital of El Salvador, in a valley below the San Salvador volcano.
Founded by the Spanish in 1525; has been damaged by many earthquakes.
Archbishop Óscar Romero, now a saint, was murdered here in 1980.
Its metro area holds over a third of the country's people.
Q311272: Municipality of Qatar, part of the Doha metropolitan area.
Hosted several 2022 FIFA World Cup venues, like Education City Stadium.
Includes Education City with branches of many foreign universities.
Q311544: The metropolitan municipality of Durban and surrounding towns in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
Created in 2000; most of its people speak isiZulu.
Durban's port is the busiest in sub-Saharan Africa.
Q3120966: City in Andhra Pradesh near the new capital region of Amaravati.
The world's largest chilli trading market is here.
Also a big centre of cotton and tobacco trade.
Q312723: The largest city of the Nile Delta's Gharbia Governorate.
Centre of Egypt's textile industry; the Misr Spinning and Weaving Company is one of the largest in Africa.
Its workers' strike in 2008 was a forerunner of the 2011 revolution.
Q3130: Capital of New South Wales and Australia's largest city, around Sydney Harbour.
Founded in 1788 as a British penal colony, the first European settlement in Australia.
The Sydney Opera House (a World Heritage Site) and Harbour Bridge are its icons; Bondi Beach is in the east.
Hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics; it is not Australia's capital (that is Canberra).
Q31356: The main city of the Swat Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
Hometown of Malala Yousafzai, the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
The Swat Valley was a centre of Gandhara Buddhism; nicknamed the 'Switzerland of Pakistan'.
Q3141: Capital of Victoria and Australia's second-largest city, on Port Phillip Bay.
Grew rich from the Victorian gold rush of the 1850s; was Australia's capital from 1901 to 1927.
Known for its laneway cafés, trams (the world's largest tram network) and sports: the Australian Open and Melbourne Cup.
Often ranked one of the world's most liveable cities.
Q31487: Poland's second city and royal capital until 1596, on the Vistula.
Its Old Town and Wawel Castle were among the first World Heritage Sites (1978); the Main Square is one of Europe's largest.
Copernicus studied at the Jagiellonian University (1364).
Nearby are the Wieliczka salt mine and the Auschwitz-Birkenau memorial.
Q3181093: Island upazila off the coast of Cox's Bazar District, Bangladesh.
Known for its lighthouse and salt production.
Very vulnerable to cyclones and erosion from the Bay of Bengal.
Q318156: City in Punjab, Pakistan, at the edge of the Cholistan Desert.
Capital of the princely state of Bahawalpur, ruled by Nawabs until 1955.
Known for its palaces, like Noor Mahal, and the Derawar Fort in the desert.
Gateway to Lal Suhanra National Park.
Q3183: Capital of Western Australia, on the Swan River near the Indian Ocean.
Often called the most isolated big city in the world (Adelaide is over 2,000 km away).
Founded in 1829 as the Swan River Colony; boomed with gold and later iron-ore mining.
Known for Kings Park and quokkas on nearby Rottnest Island.
Q319660: Capital of Kasai-Oriental province in DR Congo, one of the country's largest cities.
A centre of diamond mining: the region produces a large share of the world's industrial diamonds.
The name means 'goat water' in the Tshiluba language.
Very remote, with few paved roads connecting it to the rest of the country.
Q319804: Resort city at the southern tip of Hainan, China's tropical island.
Called the 'Hawaii of China' for its beaches like Yalong Bay.
The Guanyin of the South Sea statue (108 m) stands in the sea at Nanshan.
Hosted Miss World several times; has a big duty-free mall.
Q320704: Capital of Edo State in southern Nigeria.
Capital of the Kingdom of Benin, famous for its bronzes and once surrounded by huge earthen walls.
The British sacked the city in 1897 and took the Benin Bronzes, many of which are now being returned.
Seat of the Oba of Benin.
Q320792: The largest city of Equatorial Guinea, on the Atlantic coast of the mainland (Río Muni).
Was the country's capital at times; the official capital is Malabo on Bioko island.
Known for its seafront promenade and nightlife.
Q321079: Capital of Plateau State in central Nigeria, at about 1,200 m.
Grew with tin mining under British rule.
Has a cooler climate than most of Nigeria; the Jos Museum and wildlife park are known.
Has suffered from ethnic and religious violence.
Q321475: Ancient port city in southern Kerala on Ashtamudi Lake; formerly called Quilon.
A spice port for over 2,000 years, trading with Romans, Arabs and Chinese.
Q322155: City in northwestern Bangladesh on the Padma River, near the Indian border.
Famous for Rajshahi silk and mangoes.
Called the 'City of Education'; home of the Varendra Research Museum, Bangladesh's oldest museum.
Known as one of the cleanest and greenest cities in Bangladesh.
Q3238: Capital of Honduras, in a mountain valley; forms one capital district with Comayagüela.
Became the capital in 1880, replacing Comayagua.
Grew from a Spanish silver-mining town; the name may mean 'silver hills'.
Its airport, Toncontín, was notorious for its difficult landing (now replaced by Palmerola).
Q323801: Mozambique's third city and the main centre of the north.
Linked by road and railway to the port of Nacala and to Malawi.
Home to the Makua people; its cathedral is one of the largest in Mozambique.
Q324293: City in northern Henan; site of Yin, the last capital of the Shang dynasty.
The oracle bones, the oldest Chinese writing (about 1200 BC), were found here.
The Yinxu ruins are a World Heritage Site; home of the National Museum of Chinese Writing.
The Red Flag Canal, cut through cliffs in the 1960s, is in the prefecture.
Q326891: The East Rand metropolitan municipality in Gauteng, east of Johannesburg; the name means 'place of peace'.
Formed in 2000 from nine towns, including Germiston, Benoni, Boksburg and Kempton Park, which grew with gold mining.
Home of OR Tambo International Airport, Africa's busiest airport.
Q3274: Capital of Nicaragua, on the shore of Lake Managua.
Chosen as capital in 1852 as a compromise between rival cities León and Granada.
Destroyed by earthquakes in 1931 and 1972; the old cathedral still stands as a ruin.
Q330531: Third city of Rajasthan, on the Chambal River.
Famous as India's coaching capital: hundreds of thousands of students prepare there for engineering and medical exams.
Capital of the Kota princely state; known for Kota miniature paintings and Kota Doria saris.
Claims to be India's first traffic-light-free city.
Q3306: Capital of Panama, at the Pacific entrance of the Panama Canal.
Founded in 1519, the first Spanish city on the Pacific coast of the Americas; Inca gold passed through it.
Destroyed by the pirate Henry Morgan in 1671 and rebuilt nearby; the old Casco Viejo is a World Heritage Site.
A banking hub with Latin America's most impressive skyline.
Q330643: City in Uttar Pradesh on the Ramganga River.
Called 'Pital Nagri' (Brass City) for its brass handicrafts exported worldwide.
Founded in 1600 and named after Mughal prince Murad Bakhsh.
Q332753: The westernmost city of Shandong, formerly Caozhou.
Called the 'Peony Capital of China', with huge peony fields and a festival every April.
Associated with Song Jiang and the outlaws of 'Water Margin' in nearby Yuncheng.
Q33377: City in Indian Punjab on the Grand Trunk Road.
India's biggest sports goods manufacturing centre.
Many emigrants to the UK and Canada come from the area; called the 'NRI hub'.
Hosts the Harballabh music festival, one of the oldest in India.
Q333928: Capital of Aragua state in north-central Venezuela.
Called the 'Garden City'; the dictator Juan Vicente Gómez made it his base and built much of it.
A centre of the Venezuelan air force and aviation.
Q334: A city-state on an island at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, about 1° north of the equator.
Founded as a British trading post by Stamford Raffles in 1819.
Became independent in 1965 after being expelled from Malaysia; developed rapidly under Lee Kuan Yew.
One of the world's busiest ports and financial centres; official languages are English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil.
Q33486: Called the 'Insurance Capital of the World': Aetna, The Hartford and Travelers are based here.
Mark Twain wrote Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn while living here.
Its Hartford Courant is the oldest continuously published US newspaper.
Q336350: Capital of Sokoto State in northwestern Nigeria.
Seat of the Sokoto Caliphate founded by Usman dan Fodio in 1804.
Its Sultan is the spiritual leader of Nigeria's Muslims.
Known for leather goods: 'Morocco leather' was often made here.
Q336966: Capital of Qalyubiyya Governorate in the Nile Delta, north of Cairo.
An important railway junction between Cairo and the Delta cities.
Founded as a city in 1850; part of the Greater Cairo region.
Q337123: City in the Nile Delta on the Damietta branch.
Produces most of Egypt's aluminium cookware.
A historic Sufi centre in the Mamluk era.
Q33935: Israel's economic and tech centre, on the Mediterranean; officially Tel Aviv-Jaffa.
Founded in 1909 as a Jewish suburb of the ancient port of Jaffa; the name means 'hill of spring'.
Its 'White City' of thousands of Bauhaus buildings is a World Heritage Site.
Israel's independence was declared here in 1948; most foreign embassies are here.
Q33959: City on the French Riviera, at the foot of the Alps near Monaco and Italy.
Belonged to Savoy/Sardinia until it became French in 1860.
Famous for the Promenade des Anglais and the Carnival of Nice; Matisse and Chagall museums are here.
With Cannes, home of the film festival, it forms the Côte d'Azur urban area.
Q33986: Port city on Chile's Pacific coast and seat of the National Congress.
Its colourful hillside neighbourhoods, linked by funiculars (ascensores), are a World Heritage Site.
Was the main port of the Pacific before the Panama Canal opened in 1914.
The poet Pablo Neruda had a house here (La Sebastiana).
Q340: Quebec's largest city, on an island in the St. Lawrence River; named after Mount Royal.
Founded in 1642 as Ville-Marie; the second-largest mainly French-speaking city in the world after Paris.
Hosted Expo 67 and the 1976 Summer Olympics.
Known for its Old Town, festivals, bagels and smoked meat.
Q3426: City in southwestern Russia on the Voronezh River near the Don.
Peter the Great built Russia's first navy fleet here in 1696 for the Azov campaigns.
Heavily destroyed in WWII; a front line in 1942–43.
Known for its fertile black soil (chernozem) region.
Q34261: Capital of Haiti, on the Gulf of Gonâve.
Founded by the French in 1749; Haiti became the first independent Black republic in 1804 after a slave revolt.
Devastated by the 2010 earthquake, which killed over 200,000 people.
Large parts have been controlled by armed gangs in recent years.
Q34370: Second city of the Netherlands at the mouth of the Rhine and Meuse; Europe's largest seaport.
Its centre was destroyed by German bombing in 1940 and rebuilt with modern architecture.
Famous for the cube houses, the Erasmus Bridge and the Markthal.
The scholar Erasmus was born here.
Q34404: City in Louisiana on the Mississippi near the Gulf of Mexico; nicknamed 'The Big Easy'.
Founded by the French in 1718; its French Quarter keeps Creole architecture.
Birthplace of jazz (Louis Armstrong) and famous for Mardi Gras and Creole and Cajun food.
Devastated by Hurricane Katrina in 2005 when the levees failed.
Q34412: Prefecture-level city in Guangdong, merged into one urban area with Guangzhou in the Pearl River Delta.
Regarded as the home of Cantonese opera, southern Chinese kung fu and lion dancing.
Hometown of Wong Fei-hung, the martial artist made famous by Jackie Chan and Jet Li films.
A big manufacturing centre for ceramics, furniture and household appliances (Midea).
Q34600: Former imperial capital of Japan (794–1868), in the Kansai region.
Has about 1,600 Buddhist temples and 400 Shinto shrines; 17 sites are part of a World Heritage listing.
Famous sights include Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion), Fushimi Inari's red torii gates and the Gion geisha district.
Spared from bombing in WWII; the 1997 Kyoto Protocol on climate change was signed here.
Q34647: South Africa's largest city and economic capital, in Gauteng province on the Witwatersrand ridge.
Founded in 1886 after gold was discovered; nicknamed 'Egoli', the City of Gold.
Soweto, centre of the anti-apartheid struggle, is part of the city; Nelson Mandela lived on Vilakazi Street.
Home of Africa's largest stock exchange and of the Constitutional Court.
Q34664: Capital of Hiroshima Prefecture, on the Ōta River delta.
Destroyed by the first atomic bomb used in war on 6 August 1945.
The Atomic Bomb Dome and Peace Memorial Park are reminders; the city campaigns for nuclear disarmament.
Known for okonomiyaki and the nearby Itsukushima Shrine with its 'floating' torii gate.
Q34692: Capital of Jamaica, on a natural harbour on the southeast coast.
Founded in 1692 after an earthquake destroyed nearby Port Royal, the 'wickedest city on Earth'.
Birthplace of reggae, ska and dancehall; the Bob Marley Museum is here.
The largest English-speaking city south of the US in the Americas.
Q34750: City in northwestern Liaoning bordering Inner Mongolia.
Once had Asia's largest open-pit coal mine (Haizhou).
Known for agate carving — called China's agate capital.
Q34804: The largest city in New Mexico, on the Rio Grande below the Sandia Mountains.
Founded in 1706 as a Spanish outpost on the Camino Real.
Hosts the world's largest hot-air balloon festival every October.
Setting of the TV series 'Breaking Bad'.
Q34820: Capital of the Dominican Republic, on the south coast of Hispaniola.
Founded in 1496 by Bartholomew Columbus: the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas.
Its Colonial Zone has the first cathedral, university and fortress of the New World (World Heritage Site).
Was called Ciudad Trujillo under the dictator Trujillo (1936–1961).
Q34863: Founded in a single day in the Land Run of 22 April 1889, when settlers raced to claim land.
Site of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, the deadliest domestic terror attack in US history.
Known for cowboy culture and oil wells on the Capitol grounds.
Q34932: Capital of Queensland on the Brisbane River; Australia's third-largest city.
Founded in 1825 as a penal settlement for repeat offenders.
Known for its subtropical climate, South Bank parklands and nearby Gold Coast beaches.
Q35178: Capital of Kuwait, on Kuwait Bay at the northern end of the Persian Gulf.
Grew from a pearl-diving and trading port into an oil-rich city since the 1950s.
Occupied by Iraq in 1990, which triggered the Gulf War.
Q35381: Sri Lanka's largest city and commercial capital, on the west coast.
The official capital is neighbouring Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, where parliament moved in 1982.
A trading port used by Arabs, Portuguese, Dutch and British; capital of British Ceylon from 1815.
Its port is one of the busiest in South Asia.
Q35484: The second holiest city in Islam, in the Hejaz region of Saudi Arabia.
The Prophet Muhammad moved here from Mecca in 622 (the Hijra, start of the Islamic calendar) and is buried here.
The Prophet's Mosque (Al-Masjid an-Nabawi) is one of the largest mosques in the world.
Q35493: Kazakhstan's largest city, at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau mountains in the southeast.
Capital until 1997, when the government moved to Astana; still the economic centre.
The name means 'place of apples' — the wild ancestor of the domestic apple comes from this region.
Medeu, a high-altitude skating rink, and Shymbulak ski resort are just above the city.
Q3551: Capital of Morocco, on the Atlantic at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river, opposite Salé.
Founded by the Almohads in the 12th century; the unfinished Hassan Tower dates from then.
A base of the Barbary corsairs (the 'Republic of Salé') in the 17th century.
Became the capital under the French protectorate in 1912; the Kasbah of the Udayas and the Mausoleum of Mohammed V are landmarks.
Q3561: Capital of Algeria, on the Mediterranean; called 'Alger la Blanche' for its white buildings.
Its Casbah, the old Ottoman-era citadel, is a World Heritage Site.
A base of the Barbary corsairs; capital of French Algeria from 1830 to 1962.
Scene of the Battle of Algiers (1956–57) in the war of independence; the Notre-Dame d'Afrique and the Great Mosque of Algiers are landmarks.
Q3572: Capital of Tunisia, on the Gulf of Tunis.
The ruins of ancient Carthage, rival of Rome, lie in its suburbs.
Its medina, with the Zitouna Mosque, is a World Heritage Site.
Avenue Habib Bourguiba was the centre of the 2011 revolution that started the Arab Spring.
Q35765: Japan's third-largest city, on Osaka Bay; heart of the Keihanshin metro area with Kobe and Kyoto.
Traditionally Japan's merchant and economic hub, nicknamed 'the nation's kitchen'.
Osaka Castle was built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in the 1580s.
Known for street food such as takoyaki and okonomiyaki; hosted the 1970 and 2025 World Expos.
Q3579: Capital of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast.
Founded by the Phoenicians as Oea in the 7th century BC.
The Red Castle (Assaraya al-Hamra) and the Arch of Marcus Aurelius are landmarks.
Ruled by Ottomans and Italians; the US fought the Barbary corsairs here (the 'shores of Tripoli').
Q35997: Turkey's third city, on the Aegean coast; known in antiquity as Smyrna.
Over 3,000 years old; possibly the birthplace of Homer; ancient Ephesus is about 70 km south.
Largely burned in 1922 at the end of the Greco-Turkish war.
Considered Turkey's most liberal big city; a major port and trade-fair centre.
Q359990: City in Anhui on the Yangtze River, southwest of Nanjing.
Historically one of China's four great rice markets.
Home of the carmaker Chery and the Fantawild theme parks.
Known for iron pictures (tiehua), a local art.
Q360069: City in northern Anhui on the Huai River; the name means 'clam wharf'.
A railway junction on the Beijing–Shanghai line; near Fengyang, hometown of the first Ming emperor.
Q360178: City in Anhui on the Huai River.
Known for coal mining and power plants.
Considered the birthplace of tofu, said to have been invented by Liu An, the Han-dynasty Prince of Huainan.
Liu An's court wrote the 'Huainanzi', a classic of Chinese thought.
Q360235: Industrial city in Anhui on the Yangtze, next to Nanjing; the name means 'saddle mountain'.
Called 'Steel City' for the Masteel works.
Also called 'Poetry City': the poet Li Bai died nearby at Caishiji, where legend says he drowned trying to embrace the moon's reflection.
Q360268: Grew around coal mines since the 1950s.
Known for Kouzi liquor (baijiu) and as an ancient town of the Sui–Tang Grand Canal.
Q360326: City in southern Anhui on the Yangtze; the name means 'copper hill'.
Copper has been mined here for over 3,000 years; called 'China's ancient copper capital'.
An asteroid is named after it.
Q360374: City in southwest Anhui on the Yangtze.
Birthplace of Huangmei opera, one of China's most popular opera styles.
Hometown of Chen Duxiu, a founder of the Chinese Communist Party.
The Zhenfeng Pagoda is the city's landmark.
Q360584: City in northwestern Anhui on the Ying River.
A big agricultural and labour-exporting region.
The Song writer Ouyang Xiu governed here and loved its West Lake of Yingzhou.
Q360643: City in northern Anhui (not to be confused with Suzhou in Jiangsu).
The Grand Canal of the Sui and Tang dynasties ran through it.
Site of the Battle of Gaixia (202 BC), where Xiang Yu was defeated by Liu Bang.
Q360702: City in western Anhui at the northern foot of the Dabie Mountains.
Famous for Lu'an Guapian, a melon-seed-shaped green tea and one of China's top teas.
An old revolutionary base area of the Red Army.
Q360769: China's biggest market for traditional Chinese medicine herbs.
Hometown of Cao Cao, the Three Kingdoms warlord, and of the physician Hua Tuo.
Q3616: Capital of Iran, at the foot of the Alborz mountains; the largest city in West Asia.
Made capital in 1786 by the Qajar dynasty; it is the 51st capital in Iran's history.
Nearby ancient Rey (Rhages) is now part of the metro area.
Landmarks include the Golestan Palace, the Azadi Tower and the Milad Tower.
Q3624: Capital of Ethiopia, at about 2,355 m — the highest capital in Africa; the name means 'new flower'.
Founded in 1886 by Emperor Menelik II and his wife Taytu.
Headquarters of the African Union and the UN Economic Commission for Africa — often called the 'political capital of Africa'.
The National Museum holds 'Lucy', a 3.2-million-year-old hominin skeleton.
Q362865: City in western Jiangxi bordering Hunan.
The 1922 Anyuan coal miners' strike, led by Liu Shaoqi and Li Lisan, was an early Communist labour success.
Part of the 1927 Autumn Harvest Uprising led by Mao.
Known for fireworks and Wugong Mountain.
Q362959: Known as a steel city (Xinyu Steel) and a centre of solar-panel making (LDK).
The Fairy Lake (Xiannu Lake) is linked to the legend of the Seven Fairies.
Q3630: Capital of Indonesia, on the northwest coast of Java facing the Java Sea; its metro area is called Jabodetabek.
The Dutch East India Company rebuilt it in 1619 as Batavia, its main base in Asia; it was renamed Jakarta during the Japanese occupation.
Indonesian independence was proclaimed here in 1945.
Because Jakarta is sinking and congested, Indonesia is building a new capital, Nusantara, on Borneo.
Q36312: The largest city in Alberta, where the Bow and Elbow rivers meet near the Rocky Mountains.
Centre of the Canadian oil and gas industry.
Hosts the Calgary Stampede, a huge rodeo and festival every July.
Hosted the 1988 Winter Olympics; gateway to Banff National Park.
Q363166: City in southern Jiangxi, on the Gan River.
Its Song-dynasty city wall and a 900-year-old underground drainage system (Fushou Gou) still work.
A large Hakka area and a major producer of rare earth metals and navel oranges.
Nearby Ruijin was the capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic, starting point of the Long March.
Q363326: City in western Jiangxi; the name means 'pleasant spring'.
Home of Mount Mingyue and hot springs.
A big lithium-mining area, important for batteries.
Tradition links it to the Zen monastic rules of Baizhang.
Q363391: City in northeastern Jiangxi on the Fu River (not to be confused with Fuzhou in Fujian).
Hometown of the playwright Tang Xianzu ('The Peony Pavilion') and the reformer Wang Anshi.
Called a 'land of talents' for its many scholars.
Q363479: City in northeastern Jiangxi, where Jiangxi borders Zhejiang, Fujian and Anhui.
Mount Sanqingshan, a Taoist mountain with granite peaks, is a World Heritage Site in the prefecture.
Wuyuan county is famous for its Huizhou-style villages and rapeseed flower fields.
Q36399: City in central Vietnam on the Perfume River.
The imperial capital of the Nguyễn dynasty (1802–1945).
Its Citadel, Forbidden Purple City and royal tombs are a World Heritage Site.
Heavily damaged in the 1968 Battle of Huế; known for its spicy cuisine like bún bò Huế.
Q3640: Capital of Turkey, in central Anatolia; Turkey's second-largest city.
Known in antiquity as Ancyra; capital of the Celtic Galatians and of a Roman province.
Atatürk led the War of Independence from here and made it the capital in 1923; his mausoleum, Anıtkabir, is a landmark.
The Angora goat, cat and rabbit are named after the city's old name.
Q3642: Capital of Eritrea, at 2,325 m on the highland plateau.
Built up by the Italians as the capital of their colony; called 'Africa's Little Rome'.
Its modernist and Art Deco architecture (e.g. the Fiat Tagliero garage) is a World Heritage Site.
Known for its café culture with espresso and cappuccino.
Q36433: Portugal's second city, on the Douro River near the Atlantic.
Gave its name to Portugal ('Portus Cale') and to port wine, aged in cellars across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia.
Its historic Ribeira district is a World Heritage Site; the Dom Luís I iron bridge is a landmark.
Home of FC Porto; Henry the Navigator was born here.
Q3646: Southern Russia's largest city, on the Kuban River.
Founded in 1793 as Yekaterinodar, a fortress of the Black Sea Cossacks.
Centre of Russia's richest farming region; home of FC Krasnodar.
Gateway to the Black Sea coast resorts like Sochi.
Q365: Germany's fourth-largest city, on the Rhine.
Founded by the Romans as Colonia; its Gothic cathedral took over 600 years to complete (1248–1880).
Famous for its carnival, Kölsch beer and Eau de Cologne perfume.
About 90% destroyed in WWII; the cathedral survived.
Q36529: Capital of Alborz province, about 40 km west of Tehran at the foot of the Alborz mountains.
Iran's fourth-largest city; grew rapidly as an industrial and commuter city for Tehran.

Has a very diverse population of migrants from all over Iran.
Q3659: Capital of Chad, on the Chari River opposite Cameroon.
Founded by the French as Fort-Lamy; renamed N'Djamena in the 1970s.
Close to Lake Chad, which has shrunk dramatically.
One of the hottest capital cities in the world.
Q36600: Seat of the Dutch government and royal residence, on the North Sea coast; Amsterdam is the official capital.
Called the 'international city of peace and justice': the International Court of Justice and International Criminal Court are here.
Its Mauritshuis museum holds Vermeer's 'Girl with a Pearl Earring'.
The beach resort Scheveningen is part of the city.
Q367354: Coastal town in Kannur district, Kerala; called Tellicherry by the British.

The British East India Company built a fort here in 1708.
Famous for Thalassery biryani and Tellicherry pepper.
Q3674: Capital of Niger, on the Niger River.
Grew from small villages after the French chose it as the colonial capital in 1926.
Known for its Grand Mosque and the Niger National Museum.
One of the hottest capitals in the world.
Q36796: Twin city with Jamalpur on the Ganges in Bihar.
Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal, made it his capital and arsenal in the 1760s.
Jamalpur has one of India's oldest railway workshops (1862).
The Bihar School of Yoga is here; known for gun-making.
Q3688: Capital of Mauritania, on the Atlantic edge of the Sahara.
Built from scratch from 1958 as a capital for the new country; planned for only 15,000 people.

Sand dunes reach into the city; its fish market is famous.
Q3692: Capital of Saudi Arabia, on the Najd plateau in the centre of the Arabian Peninsula.
Taken by Ibn Saud in 1902, the start of the conquest that created Saudi Arabia.

Diriyah, the original Saudi capital and a World Heritage Site, is on its edge; Riyadh will host Expo 2030.
Q36947: Capital of Bahia, founded in 1549 as the first capital of colonial Brazil (until 1763).

Has one of the biggest street carnivals in the world.
Q3703: Capital of Mali, on the Niger River.
The name means 'crocodile river' in Bambara; the crocodile is the city's symbol.
Grew from a small town into a French colonial capital (1908) and is now one of Africa's fastest-growing cities.
Known for its music scene (e.g. Salif Keïta, Amadou & Mariam).
Q37100: New Zealand's largest city, on a narrow isthmus between two harbours.
Built on a field of about 50 volcanoes, like Mount Eden and Rangitoto Island.
Nicknamed the 'City of Sails' for its many boats; hosted the America's Cup.
Has the largest Polynesian population of any city in the world.
Q3711: Capital of Serbia, where the Sava flows into the Danube; the name means 'White City'.
One of the oldest cities in Europe, near the Vinča culture sites.

Capital of Yugoslavia during the 20th century.
Q3718: Capital of Senegal, on the Cap-Vert peninsula — the westernmost point of mainland Africa.
Capital of French West Africa from 1902.

Known for the African Renaissance Monument and as the old finish of the Paris–Dakar Rally.
Q372414: City on the Yellow River delta on the Bohai Sea coast of Shandong.
Built around the Shengli Oil Field, China's second-largest.
The Yellow River Delta wetland reserve is a major bird habitat.
Q372773: Capital of Chhattisgarh, which was created in 2000.
A big centre of steel, power and the rice trade.
Next to Naya Raipur, a new planned capital city.
Q372791: City in southwestern Shandong on the Grand Canal.
